hybrids.rationale: Dairy, meat, ready-meal and bakery facilities frequently combine cold-chain storage with on-site thermal processing (cook, pasteurize, retort, sanitation steam). Process heat and refrigeration coexist by design; flagging process patterns as contamination would block valid cross-system intelligence.

Modern omnichannel DCs combine ambient, refrigerated and frozen zones in a single building. Cold-chain patterns apply to the conditioned zones without invalidating warehouse logic (MHE charging, dock cycles).
Class-A office buildings increasingly house edge DC or telco hub tenants. The DC load and cooling topology must be characterized independently from the office HVAC schedule, but coexist in one asset.

Plants with attached finished-goods warehouses (FMCG, automotive Tier-1, building products) present both process loads and DC loads in one footprint. Warehouse patterns are legitimate when the DC is operationally distinct from production lines.

Mixed-use commercial buildings hosting supermarkets, food retail, or commercial kitchens carry refrigeration loads that dominate base electrical consumption. Refrigeration logic applies despite the dominant office/retail building envelope.
